metadata.title: Profiles of academic performance and perceived digital distraction in secondary classrooms

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2022 microdata for 15-year-old students from 30 participating education systems and applies the final student weight W_FSTUWT for weighted descriptive statistics and for weighted one-way ANOVA/Balanced Repeated Replication (BRR) checks of cluster separation. For the clustering ensemble stage, the authors explicitly incorporate sampling weights (W_FSTUWT) to improve representativeness and stability across plausible values and random initializations. In the classification stage, the paper does not state that survey weights are incorporated into the XGBoost training; instead it uses a strict within-fold preprocessing pipeline (RobustScaler, SMOTE-Tomek) and evaluates with stratified 5-fold cross-validation, which is typical for ML workflows that do not natively support complex survey weights. Therefore, while weights are used for clustering validation and descriptive representativeness, the predictive performance metrics should be interpreted as model-based discrimination rather than fully design-weighted population estimates.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2022 student microdata for 15-year-old students with mathematics as the major domain, restricted to 30 participating education systems that administered the selected predictors (from the Student Questionnaire and the optional ICT Familiarity Questionnaire). The analytic dataset was further restricted to students with available values for the clustering variables and the 30 predictors after applying an iterative imputation procedure (MICE) to address missingness. For the clustering outcome, mathematics performance was represented by the ten mathematics plausible values (PV1MATH–PV10MATH), and digital distraction was operationalized using ST273Q06 with reverse coding and group-mean centering (DIGDIST_L1) at the school level (DIGDIST_L2 computed but not used as the clustering variable).

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics (15-year-olds; PV1MATH–PV10MATH; school-level centered digital distraction)
main_findings.target_variable: Profile membership: Clu_2 (High-Distraction Low-Achievers) vs Clu_1 (Low-Distraction High-Achievers)
main_findings.performance_metrics: XGBoost (5-fold CV): Accuracy 0.946 (0.000), AUC 0.984 (0.001), Precision 0.926 (0.005), F1 0.911 (0.001), Recall (Target) 0.968 (0.003). Additional analysis (Profile membership: Clu_3 (Low-Distraction Low-Achievers) vs Clu_1 (Low-Distraction High-Achievers)): XGBoost (5-fold CV): Accuracy 0.822 (0.003), AUC 0.913 (0.001), Precision 0.797 (0.007), F1 0.842 (0.002), Recall (Target) 0.893 (0.010). Additional analysis (Profile membership: Clu_4 (High-Distraction High-Achievers) vs Clu_1 (Low-Distraction High-Achievers)): XGBoost (5-fold CV): Accuracy 0.852 (0.005), AUC 0.918 (0.002), Precision 0.785 (0.025), F1 0.769 (0.005), Recall (Target) 0.899 (0.019). Additional analysis (Profile membership: Clu_3 (Low-Distraction Low-Achievers) vs Clu_2 (High-Distraction Low-Achievers)): XGBoost (5-fold CV): Accuracy 0.896 (0.003), AUC 0.950 (0.002), Precision 0.858 (0.007), F1 0.843 (0.005), Recall (Reference) 0.930 (0.004). Additional analysis (Profile membership: Clu_4 (High-Distraction High-Achievers) vs Clu_2 (High-Distraction Low-Achievers)): XGBoost (5-fold CV): Accuracy 0.804 (0.003), AUC 0.898 (0.002), Precision 0.773 (0.007), F1 0.824 (0.002), Recall (Reference) 0.881 (0.010)
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Mathematics the study leveraged peer distraction exposure, classroom discipline, math self-efficacy, math anxiety, and digital self-efficacy to classify students as belonging to the high-distraction low-achiever profile versus the low-distraction high-achiever profile, finding that unfavorable external conditions and weaker internal resources most strongly distinguish Clu_2 from Clu_1. This indicates that classroom-level management of peer digital behavior and targeted self-efficacy/anxiety supports may be effective levers for reducing the risk of low achievement among highly distraction-susceptible students, though the results are predictive (not causal) and rely on cross-sectional PISA data.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2022 microdata for 15-year-old students from 30 education systems (N=239,695; 8,826 schools) with mathematics as the major domain. Mathematics achievement is represented by ten plausible values (PV1MATH–PV10MATH), and digital distraction is measured using the single PISA item ST273Q06 with reverse coding and school-level group-mean centering to form DIGDIST_L1. After MICE-based iterative imputation (LightGBM estimators), the authors identify four student profiles via a weighted cluster ensemble (k=4) and then classify profile membership using XGBoost with SMOTE-Tomek inside a stratified 5-fold cross-validation pipeline. Across five pairwise comparisons, XGBoost achieves high discrimination (Accuracy 0.804–0.946; AUC 0.898–0.984; F1 0.769–0.911). SHAP is used for interpretation, but feature importance is not causal; additionally, the paper does not indicate design-weighted training for the ML models, so predictive performance should be interpreted as classification accuracy rather than population-level effects.
